guard_returns_true.meaning: validatePrice() unconditionally returns true, allowing the downstream guard to pass even when spot deviation would exceed the caller-supplied slippage tolerance

claims.scope: UniswapPriceOracle TWAP validation of Uniswap V2 spot prices and downstream swap/liquidity operations

preconditions.text: The oracle reads cumulativePriceLast from the Uniswap V2 pair as a single cumulative-price snapshot.; validatePrice() receives a caller-supplied slippage tolerance as maxSlippage.

safety.derivation: Program synthesis from the selected intent and logical pattern.

effects.text: The validatePrice() guard always passes even when spot deviation would exceed the slippage tolerance.
effects.derivation: Program-generated direct negation witness for the selected safety pattern.

assumptions: validatePrice() is called as a pre-swap or pre-liquidity guard by downstream callers, as stated for IOracle(poolOracle).validatePrice(maxSlippage).
A correct TWAP requires two cumulative-price snapshots separated in time, so a single-snapshot reading cannot provide a genuine TWAP.

limitations: The chosen relation formalizes only the guard-always-passes impact for validatePrice(); zero_protection_removal, arbitrary_price_swaps and attacker_profit are deferred to future claims.
No concrete on-chain transaction, executed flashloan incident, or numeric expected-versus-actual oracle output is reported, so the plan remains a capability-level semantic binding.

The precondition terms both reuse the same violation-invocation trigger symbol because cumulative_price_read and caller_supplied_tolerance jointly identify the same before-state; this is intentional evidence linkage, not a self-comparison.
